expectations.text: Sets access-token TTL at roughly 1 hour and identifies ~1 hour as the cross-provider convergence point rather than an invented number.
expectations.evidence: 1 h access tokens are the cross-provider convergence point.

expectations.text: Makes refresh-token rotation with token-family reuse detection the default posture.
expectations.evidence: Refresh token | rotate every use

expectations.text: States that a reused refresh token revokes the entire token family, not only the token presented.
expectations.evidence: Reuse should kill the grant family

expectations.text: Requires a reuse grace window from day one, with a starting value in the range of roughly 10 to 30 seconds.
expectations.evidence: A 10–30 s grace window keeps false positives down

expectations.text: Justifies the grace window by legitimate concurrent refreshes (multi-tab SPAs, retries, reconnects) otherwise reading as attacks and logging real users out.
expectations.evidence: two tabs or a network retry presenting the same just-consumed token

expectations.text: Names the tension between hashing refresh tokens at rest and having to recognize a just-consumed token inside the grace window.
expectations.evidence: Django OAuth Toolkit documents this tension

expectations.text: Resolves that tension deliberately (for example by retaining the predecessor's hash with a validity timestamp) instead of abandoning hash-at-rest.
expectations.evidence: Resolve it by keeping the predecessor's hash, not by dropping hashing.

expectations.text: Caps the SPA's refresh-token lifetime far harder than the others, citing something like a 24-hour SPA lifetime against ~90-day inactivity elsewhere.
expectations.evidence: 24 h browser cap and the 90-day idle limit come from Microsoft

expectations.text: Treats the partner server-side clients as confidential clients whose client authentication already sender-constrains redemption, making non-rotating refresh tokens defensible there.
expectations.evidence: Says optional under 2.1 for confidential but applies rotation anyway; no client-authentication sender-constraint reasoning

expectations.text: States that OAuth 2.1 mandates sender-constrained or rotated refresh tokens specifically for public clients.
expectations.evidence: OAuth 2.1 requires sender-constrained or rotated refresh tokens for public clients

expectations.text: Rules out an indefinitely reusable refresh token for the public SPA client entirely, rather than offering it as a weaker option.
expectations.evidence: Rotation is mandatory for the SPA

expectations.text: Ties JWT access-token TTL to the fact that a JWT cannot be revoked mid-lifetime the way an opaque database-backed token can.
expectations.evidence: If you issue JWTs instead, the short TTL is your only revocation mechanism.
